<!--
Copy&paste links: to Jira ticket, other PRs, issues, Slack conversations...
For code bumps: link to PR, tag or GitHub `/compare/master...master`
-->

Test&Review
------------
Test cases covered:
* DescribeConfigs
* Alter the log level with and without validateOnly, validate the results with DescribeConfigs

Open questions / Follow ups
--------------------------
If you're a reviewer, I'd appreciate your thoughts on these questions I have open:
1. Should we add synchronization to the Log4jController methods? - Seems like we don't get much value from it
2. Should we instantiate a new Log4jController instead of it having static methods? - All operations are stateless, so I thought static methods would do well
3. A logger which does not have a set value returns "null" (as seen in the unit tests). Should we just return the Root logger's level?

review_comments.body:
My thinking was the following:
`ConfigType` is defined in `kafka.server` and is related to the back-end functionality - it is the names of the zNodes. The javadoc says this as well:
```
/**
 * Represents all the entities that can be configured via ZK
 */
```
The new config type I'm adding called `"broker-loggers"` is only used in the front-end - that tool is the only class that uses it. I thought it would be more confusing if we had it in kafka.server rather than just define it in the command itself.
Now, when it comes to defining it in the command we could just have a separate variable called `brokerLoggerConfigType` but I also wanted to add two lists for validating zk-only allowed configs and broker-only allowed configs:
```scala
    val zkSupportedTypes = Seq(Topic, Client, User, Broker)
    val brokerSupportedTypes = Seq(Broker, BrokerLogger)
```
Those make sense to be in the back-end though.

I also thought that coupling the front-end flags with the back-end is more brittle, even if we are super unlikely to ever change a zNode path.
I don't think it'll be too confusing for new people as they can see that the one is defined and used entirely in the tools class whereas the other `ConfigType` is used throughout.

Regardless of the wall of text, I don't feel strongly about this :D. Let me know what you think after I explained my reasoning

review_comments.body:
I had left it as `null` since that is what our current Log4jController did and to keep the scope of interface changes low. It would be inconsistent if the MBean returned "null" and the API "not set"

Let's decide on this.
* "not set" - it's just a matter of naming and I agree this is more human readable. I agree we shouldn't leave it as "null" in any case
* root logger - I prefer this. I don't think this will be confusing. If anything, it will be more informative. In practice, if not set explicitly it should always reflect the root logger (unless some crazy hierarchy was configured in log4.properties I guess). As a user, if I see `null` or `not set` I would need to **know** and fetch the root logger.
I think that this is a better approach and I also think that we should apply this to the Log4j MBean as well.

I can update the KIP, mention in the vote thread and we can be good to go.
LMK what you think

That is what we are testing, yes. This is a bit of a sanity check to see it behaves as expected and also serves as a bit of test-documentation such that anybody reading the code can see a quick example of the API.

Regarding the config source, it should (and is, as tested) be the DYNAMIC_BROKER_LOGGER_CONFIG. I found this out during implementation and mentioned in the vote thread:
```
During implementation, I noticed a couple of holes in the KIP and did the following changes:
* add a new ConfigResource - DYNAMIC_BROKER_LOGGER_CONFIG
* DELETE operations in the IncrementalAlterConfigRequest will change the logger's level to the ROOT logger's currently-set level. (we previously thought we could return to the default - log4j does not seem to allow us to do that)
```

The key being I previously thought we had a way of knowing the default but we don't, therefore the server can't return a specific config source mentioning it's a default. Adds the DYNAMIC_BROKER_LOGGER_CONFIG ConfigSource

Add Log4jController#loggers

Also refactors the class to be public
Update DescribeConfigs to work with broker logger configs

Implement IncrementalAlterConfigs for broker loggers

Adds a LogLevelConfig public class, which specifies all the supported log levels
Adds a test which makes sure the new API uses the AlterConfigs Cluster resource
Adds exhaustive tests for the IncrementalAlterConfigs change

ConfigCommand: Add broker-logger validations

Should only support --bootstrap-server and not support "entity-default"
Adds new EntityType object class
ConfigCommand: Add broker logger functionality and tests
Minor polish up
Fix header issue
Use different loggers in integration tests to ensure test isolation

Address PR comments:

- Move default values to the bottom for better convention
- Remove ALL log level
- Make some code comments clearer
- Add two tests for the new config command and entity-default behavior
- Check for entity-type/entity-default mandatory presence with --bootstrap-server in checkArgs()

Re-order Config Source enum
Add brokerId validation to ConfigCommand

Return the ROOT logger's level if an explicit log level is not set for a logger

We now return this from the Log4jController MBean as well
Remove ConfigCommand#EntityType and continue using ConfigType
Fix tests to obey broker entity name validation and add test for the validation
Clean up log levels in admin client integration test
Correctly tear down loggers in integration test

Ensure AdminClient requests go to the correct BROKER_LOGGER node

Fix test flakiness - make log4j AuthorizerIntegrationTest reset a log level rather than set
Rename some occurrences of reset to unset/remove in regards to log levels
